name: Bruce Springsteen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Bruce Springsteen, a.k.a. The Boss, spun his New Jersey, blue-collar upbringing into a substantial fortune from five decades of touring and recording.
Springsteen and his E Street Band met playing clubs along the Jersey Shore, most famously at Asbury Park's The Stone Pony.
He's sold over 140 million albums globally, with 21 studio albums, 10 live albums and seven EPs.
Accolades include 20 Grammys, an Oscar, two Golden Globes, a special Tony award and inductions in both the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Songwriters Hall of Fame.
In 2021, Springsteen sold his music catalog--his life's work--to longtime label home Sony for a $500 million lump sum.

name: Charles Zhengyao Lu
forbes_bio: A serial entrepreneur, Charles Lu founded rental car company Car Inc. in 2007 and guided it to an IPO on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2014.
But his most valuable holding is Luckin Coffee, an upstart coffee chain with ambitions of surpassing Starbucks in China.
Started by a former executive of Lu's, Luckin Coffee expanded from one shop to over 3,600 locations in two years, and listed in the U.S. in May 2019.
Lu, who helped fund the company as an angel investor, now chairs the board and owns 26% of the shares.
He still chairs Car Inc. and also runs UCar, a ride hailing startup launched in 2015.

name: Michael McCain
forbes_bio: Michael McCain is the CEO of Maple Leaf Foods, a Canadian packaged meat company that made $3.1 billion in sales in 2019.
McCain's father, Wallace McCain, cofounded frozen food company McCain Foods with his brother Harrison in 1956.
The family bought a controlling stake in Maple Leaf Foods in 1995.
In January 2020, Michael McCain grabbed headlines for his scathing tweets about then-U.S. President Donald Trump and his foreign policy.

name: Parakramsinh Jadeja
forbes_bio: Prakramsinh Jadeja is chairman and managing director of CNC machine maker Jyoti CNC Automation based in Rajkot, a city in the western Indian state of Gujarat.
He co-founded Jyoti CNC in 1989 as Jyoti Enterprises.
The company has installed 130,000 machines across 60 countries to date.
Jyoti supplies its machines to the defence, aerospace, infrastructure and auto industries.
Jadeja listed the company in January 2024 at a 12% premium to the IPO price.
forbes_facts: Jadeja is a director on the board of the Indian Machine Tools Manufacturers Association.
His company has subsidiaries in France, Germany, Canada and Turkey and a research team in France.

name: Sheela Gautam
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2018); Hurun India (2017-2018)
forbes_bio: Born in a family of diplomats, Sheela Gautam set up Sheela Foam in 1971, best known known for its Sleepwell brand of mattresses.
The $270 million (revenue) company was listed in 2016.
Her son Rahul runs Sheela Foam as chairman and managing director.
forbes_facts: Sheela Foam owns Joyce Foam in Australia.
A member of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, she was elected to parliament for four consecutive terms from 1991.

name: Candido Pinheiro Koren de Lima
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2019-2024); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Pinheiro Koren de Lima, an oncologist, used money he saved from his medical practice to launch a hospital in the Brazilian city of Fortaleza in 1986.
Over the years, he added more hospitals, then health clinics and eventually health insurance, creating what is now known as Grupo Hapvida.
He took Hapvida public in April 2018 on the Sao Paulo stock exchange; his fortune now includes stakes held by his wife and his two sons.
He is Hapvida's chairman; his son Jorge is the statutory chief executive officer, while his other son Candido Junior is a member of the board of directors.
The company has 25 hospitals and operates in over 15 Brazilian states.

name: Hari Krishan Agarwal
forbes_bio: Hari Kishan Agarwal chairs Delhi-based Campus Activewear, a leading producer of sports shoes in India.
The company sold19.3 million pairs in fiscal 2022 notching up $158 million in revenue. It has five factories across India.
Agarwal became a billionaire after the company's IPO. The  stock was listed in May 2022 at a 23% premium to the IPO price.
His son, Nikhil Aggarwal, who studied industrial engineering at Purdue University, runs the company as CEO.
forbes_facts: Private equity firm TPG and Anil Rai Gupta, who runs electrical products firm Havells, hold stakes in Campus.
Agarwal is a first-generation entrepreneur, who started out in 1983 selling sports shoes branded 'Action'.
